constraints: Every spacing value — padding, margin, gap, row and panel height, column width — is a multiple of 8, at every level of the design. 4px is a permitted half-step; type, 1px borders and radii are exempt. Written up in DESIGN-RULES.md.
Panel and column positions are constants; content scrolls inside its own box rather than growing it; scroll gutters are reserved.
Nothing drifts, floats or animates on its own. Transitions are colour and opacity only, on direct interaction.
Every claim carries a credible reference with a link so it can be verified.
Summaries quote the source verbatim rather than paraphrasing it.

feedback.title: An atlas of blood, not another lab viewer
feedback.quote: What we don't have is a model of the blood system itself. We don't know what other markers surround a result, what hasn't been measured, what should be measured next, or how biomarkers relate to one another across physiology.
quotes: We already have good tools for seeing individual blood tests—and simple trends over time.

Imagine a map instead of a list. Every blood marker exists within networks: inflammation, immunity, kidney function, metabolism, liver health, hormones, nutrition, coagulation, cancer, infection, genetics, and more. We need the “solar system” of blood markers, not isolated planets.
The most valuable information may be what's missing. Which tests have never been ordered? Which families of tests are incomplete? … Missing data is itself clinical information.
This is fundamentally a decision-space design problem.

More data isn't the problem. Claude Shannon taught us that information reduces uncertainty. The challenge is designing interfaces that transform more information into better decisions instead of more confusion.

The issue isn't the data itself. The problem is that we haven't designed an effective way for clinicians and patients to navigate it—to surface what's important, summarize the signals, expose the gaps, and reveal the relationships.
The product isn't another lab viewer. It's a decision engine.

The goal isn't simply to display blood work. It's to make the invisible structure of human physiology visible enough that clinicians and patients can ask better questions, order better tests, and make better decisions.
did: A map instead of a list
The atlas screen shows all 17 families as a packed map sized by what is inside them, replacing a landing page whose only promise was 6,192 rows.
The hero leads with 26 of 6,192 — what a routine annual panel measures against what is measurable. The stat strip shows three gaps instead of three totals.
The gap map takes what you have had drawn and returns per-family coverage. 14 of 17 families are untouched by a standard annual panel.
All six are on the landing as navigation, each honestly labelled. Two work; two are prototypes; one is evidenced for three panels only; one is not built.
Only the three routine panels are modelled as sets. Nothing else in the catalogue is grouped by “ordered together”.
Not built, and deliberately not faked. Only 6 of 6,192 markers carry a link to another family, so the map draws no edges and says so.
Blocked on the same missing relationship layer. The one worked example (iron-deficiency anemia) is hand-authored in condition-lens.html.
Screen-then-confirm exists as a prototype for one condition, not as a general capability.
Not built. Named as not built on the landing rather than quietly omitted.
What each biomarker means, with evidence
All 6,192 carry a description and a link, but only 216 are quoted from a named authority; 5,976 were AI-written from the LOINC name. The ratio is on the front door.
feedback.open: The relationship layer is the blocker for three of the points above. The fix is two small additions alongside tests — a sets array for “these are ordered together” and an edges array for reflex links like low MCV → ferritin — each carrying its own quoted or reasoned source. Scoped in §5 of INDEX-REFINEMENT.md. Until it exists, any marker-level ripple view would be drawing edges that are not in the data.

changes: Follow-ups centred on their concern row at a 24px pitch, with a tick on the anchor row. They were previously centred in the column, which is why they started mid-page.
Pill rebuilt on the 8px system — 24px tall, 8px padding per segment, 96px column, 32px rows. No more clipped words.
Non-scrolling column header labels the marker column and the three toggle segments.
Rail widened to 320px (8×40) so the padded pill does not squeeze the marker names.
Source badge moved off the map into the detail list and tooltip, so each follow-up is one line and the block stays short enough to centre.
Verified at six window sizes: zero label overlaps, zero overflow, out-dots clear of text, 92–96% width and 99–100% height in use.
versions.note: Centring clamps for concerns in the top ~130px, where a centred block would run off the canvas. Unavoidable; the anchor tick keeps the relationship readable.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — right-side connectors
versions.summary: Concern rows gain a second connector dot on their right edge, and the follow-up edges leave from there instead of sweeping back across the label text.
changes: 47 right-hand connector dots, one per concern row, at the right edge of the column.
Follow-up edges originate at the out-dot rather than the left-hand dot, so no curve crosses a label.
The out-dot is quiet grey until its row is the one feeding the third column, then warm and filled.
Marker-count chip moved inboard to clear the new dot; label clip widths re-measured.
Verified at six window sizes: zero label overlaps, zero overflow, out-dots clear of all text.
versions.note: Only the concern column changed. Markers already had their dot on the outgoing side, and follow-up tests already had theirs on the incoming side.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — three columns
versions.summary: Static, deterministic, and dense: panel markers, concerns and follow-up tests as three fixed columns filling the whole canvas. No physics, no drift, no animation.
changes: Force simulation deleted. Layout is a pure function of state and window size.
Three fixed columns — 26 panel markers grouped by CBC / CMP / lipid, all 47 concerns, and the follow-up tests for whichever concern is open.
Every row is labelled. Full marker names, full concern names, no culling.
Barycentre ordering puts each concern beside the markers that point at it, so edges run flat rather than crossing.
A drawn divider separates the 18 concerns the annual panel can reach from the 29 it cannot.
Type scales with row height and clips to its column: zero label overlaps and zero overflow at 1200×700 through 2560×1400.
Space used: 99–100% of the height, 91–96% of the width.
versions.note: Supersedes both v2.0 (fixed rings) and v2.1 (force layout). The rail, detail panel and the 29 sourced relationship notes are unchanged.

versions.title: Ripple atlas — organic layout
versions.summary: The ripple map stops being a fixed ring and becomes a live force simulation: nodes float, live concerns pull inward, dormant ones drift to the edge, and labels are placed only where they fit.
changes: Force simulation replaces the fixed rings. A radial band per role, concerns sprung toward the markers that implicate them, universal repulsion, hard collision correction, and a boundary that keeps every node out of the panels.
Live concerns come forward, dormant ones recede. The 47 concerns no longer each hold a permanent ring slot — the ones in play grow and move inward where there is room to label them.

Greedy label placement. Labels are sorted by importance and take the first of four candidate positions that collides with nothing. Zero label overlaps at 1200×700 through 1920×1080, in every interaction state.
Elliptical bands so the layout fills a wide rectangle instead of inscribing a circle in it.
Ambient drift — per-node phase, slow breathing motion, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Flowing dash on live edges so the ripple visibly travels outward from a marker you flag.
Node overlaps: zero once settled, at every size tested.
versions.note: Motion is confined to the map canvas. The rails, detail slots and scroll gutters stay fixed, so this does not undo the no-shift guarantee from v2.0.

versions.title: Ripple atlas
versions.summary: A different route into the atlas: start from the 26 markers of a routine annual panel, mark what came back abnormal, and watch the ripple spread into concerns and the tests that would follow them up.
changes: Three concentric rings. Inner: the 26 annual-panel markers, grouped by CBC / CMP / lipid. Middle: all 47 concerns, each holding a permanent slot. Outer: the follow-up tests for whichever concern is open.
Mark low or high on any panel marker and the concerns it can represent light up, with edges coloured by direction.
29 sourced relationship notes — every one a verbatim MedlinePlus (NIH) quote with a verify link, re-checked against the source pages after authoring.
Personal concern layer. The 29 concerns a routine panel cannot reach can be added by hand; one that no panel marker touches says so outright.

Nothing moves. Ring geometry is computed once per window size and cached; interactions change colour and opacity only. Scroll areas reserve their gutters. Verified by diffing every circle coordinate across marking, selecting and adding.
Marker radius derived from the ring chord, so the 26 inner circles cannot overlap at any window size. Checked at 1200×700 through 1920×1080.
95 KB standalone — no 6,192-row table, so it loads instantly.
versions.note: This is an alternative to the v1.1 family atlas, not a replacement. v1.1 maps the whole catalogue by family; v2.0 starts from what you have actually had done. Both are candidates.

versions.title: Atlas cockpit — fixed panels
versions.summary: The atlas stops being a scrolling page and becomes a fixed cockpit: the map fills the viewport, everything else floats above it, nothing ever reflows.
changes: Nothing scrolls or resizes. The stage is fixed; panels are absolutely positioned and hold their dimensions. Anything that could overflow scrolls inside its own box instead of growing.
Map is the ground plane. It fills the viewport behind four floating glass panels — controls and family index on the left, detail on the right, legend and the honesty line along the bottom.
Circles never jump. Positions are packed once per stage size and cached; toggling shade or re-ordering the index only re-paints colour. Verified by diffing circle coordinates across a shade toggle.

Packing is area-conserving — circles scale to fill ~46% of whatever space the panels leave, so the map uses the room it has at any window size. Panel footprints are measured, not guessed, so no circle hides under a panel.
Detail panel is always mounted at a fixed size. With nothing selected it shows the whole-atlas summary; selecting a family swaps the content without changing the box.
Drill-in is an overlay sheet that fades over the map — every marker in the family, filterable, each linking to its LOINC record. Esc or the scrim closes it.
Index and map cross-highlight on hover; clicking either selects, clicking again deselects.
No dimming of unselected families. The shape of what is unmeasured is the point of the map, so it stays readable while you inspect one family.
versions.note: The family-card grid from v1.0 is gone — the index rail and detail panel replace it. Landing and gap map are unchanged.

versions.title: Atlas rebuild
versions.summary: Landing reframed from a navigation question into a claim, plus two new screens: a gap map and a family atlas.
changes: Hero states the thesis. “Where do you want to start?” becomes “There are 6,192 things that can be measured in your blood. A routine annual checkup measures 26.”

Stat strip shows gaps, not totals. The volume pair (6,192 tests · 17 body systems) is replaced by 26 of 6,192 in a routine panel, 1,602 markers no symptom reaches, and 4 of 17 families with no quoted source.
New gap map (#cxGaps) — mark the panels you’ve had, search in individual markers, see per-family coverage. Persists to localStorage.
New family atlas (#cxAtlas) — 17 family cards, shade by routine-panel or source coverage, sort by size / least covered / A–Z.
Six-question spine on the landing, each labelled built / prototype / partial / not built.
Family map generated from the payload by deterministic circle packing. No edges drawn, because only 6 of 6,192 markers carry a link to another family.
Honesty band — 216 quoted entries vs 5,976 AI-written, with source names read out of the data.
Fixed two bugs found in testing: [].slice.call() on a Set returns empty, which had silently broken the added-markers list and localStorage persistence.
versions.note: Every figure is computed from the payload at load, so the copy cannot drift from the dataset. Regenerate with pipeline/build_v2.py.

versions.title: Free-text symptom search
versions.summary: The last state of the original dashboard before the atlas rebuild. This is the roll-back target if the atlas goes wrong.
changes: Free-text search on the condition explorer home (cxFeelSearch) with fuzzy matching into concern chips.
“Search all tests” escape hatch from the search results into the table view.
Feedback link added to the dashboard header.
Blood-fill animation on the landing figure retuned (cxrise 120px → 185px).
versions.note: These edits were uncommitted when the atlas work began; committed as their own milestone so this exact state stays recoverable.

versions.title: Polished landing and table toolbar
versions.summary: Visual pass on the two-door landing and usability work on the all-tests table.
changes: Landing figure with the blood-fill mask, animated leader lines to each route card, and live card stats read from the dataset.
Per-system mini bar chart on the “Explore all tests” card.
Table toolbar: expand all, collapse all, back to top, and a sticky toolbar dock.
Rollup system bar with legend in the dashboard header.

versions.title: Condition explorer prototype
versions.summary: The biggest single change in the project's history: conditions become a first-class object sitting between symptoms and tests.
changes: Route landing (#cxRoute) with two doors — start from how you feel, or explore all tests.
Condition explorer (#cxApp): symptom → candidate conditions → condition lens.
Condition lens with ripple diagram, “have you had this?” checklist, path-to-diagnosis track and a locked miniDx card.
All-tests table view with name / system / source filters.
Added condition-lens.html, IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md and the pipeline/ source files.
versions.note: This is the version IMPROVEMENT-PLAN.md was written against.

versions.title: Initial dashboard
versions.summary: The original concern-in, test-list-out tool. No conditions, no landing page, no table view.
changes: 6,192-test catalogue with the concern picker and age / sex / life-stage / medication filters.
Rollup stat strip and callouts.
“Worth asking your doctor about” ranking, and annual-panel coverage against what sits outside it.
Source-quoted vs AI-generated badges throughout.
